reason: The hypothesis combines the dynamic amorphization and inverse Hall-Petch wear mechanism from P3/P4 (CoCrFeMnNi in inert UHV) with the B-microalloying grain refinement and passive film stabilization from P1/P9/P11 (AlCoCrFeNiMoTi in separate wear and corrosion tests) and proposes their synergistic coupling in a simultaneous wear-corrosion environment, a link that neither passage makes. It transfers the amorphization concept to a different alloy system and a corrosive environment, and proposes a controlled comparison to test the synergy, which goes beyond the separate findings of the cited papers.
copied_elements: B microalloying to refine microstructure and improve wear/corrosion resistance in AlCoCrFeNiMoTi (P1, P2, P9, P11)
Shear-induced formation of ultra-nanocrystalline/near-amorphous surface layer in CoCrFeMnNi (P3, P4, P10, P40, P43)
Inverse Hall-Petch behavior and low friction/wear linked to amorphous layer (P3, P4, P10, P40, P43)
Rapid re-passivation and passive film stability from refined microstructure (P1, P11, P13, P18, P25, P26)
Combined wear-corrosion testing with OCP monitoring and electrochemical measurements (P18, P19, P25, P26)
Post-test SEM/TEM to verify nanocrystalline/amorphous layer (P3, P4, P10, P40)
